attempts.summary: Restricted cron job scheduling on node1 (Alpine Linux, busybox crond) to only root and opsadmin. Since busybox's crontab does not support /etc/cron.allow /etc/cron.deny and its setuid helper (bbsuid) grants root escalation to any user invoking /usr/bin/crontab, I replaced /usr/bin/crontab with a wrapper script that checks the calling user against an allowlist (root, opsadmin) before delegating to the real bbsuid-backed crontab applet (relocated to /usr/lib/cron-helper/bbsuid-crontab, invoked with argv0=/usr/bin/crontab so bbsuid's hardcoded path dispatch still matches). Created the opsadmin user. Verified root and opsadmin can create/list/remove crontabs while other users (alpine, nobody) are denied with a clear error. Restarted node1 via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed (3f62700c... -> 6c2ecdfb...), and re-verified after restart that the wrapper, opsadmin account, root's original system crontab (periodic run-parts jobs), and the access restriction all persisted and function correctly. Cleaned up all test crontab entries left over from verification.
